supporters.quote: 'Relative alpha2 power and alpha2/alpha1 ratio were significantly lower in PD-MCI and AD-MCI groups compared to HC, whereas no significant differences were observed for these spectral parameters between these two pathological groups. In addition, the relative alpha1 sub-band power was significantly higher in AD-MCI than in HC group. No significant differences for relative alpha band power were found between three groups.' (p. 3); 'keeping the integrity of global alpha rhythm in both neurodegenerative diseases' (p. 5)
supporters.note: Trieste hd-EEG, N = 36 (15 AD-MCI, 11 PD-MCI, 10 HC). The reduction is confined to relative high alpha (alpha2, 10.5 to 13 Hz) and the alpha2/alpha1 ratio; total relative alpha power did not differ (p = 0.214) and alpha1 was higher in AD-MCI than controls, which the authors read as a redistribution within the alpha band, not a loss of alpha. Supports a narrower form: reduced upper-alpha power in AD-MCI and PD-MCI. Bonferroni-adjusted p-values are reported (alpha2: AD-MCI vs HC adj. p = 0.009; PD-MCI vs HC adj. p < 0.001), contrary to the record's statement that no block reports adjusted p-values. All but one AD-MCI patient took AChE inhibitors and PD-MCI were recorded 'on' levodopa. Also reports an alpha-derived difference between aetiologies (alpha/theta lower in PD-MCI than AD-MCI).

supporters.quote: '(1) all MCI groups over the HC group showed decreased occipital rsEEG alpha power density' (p. 1); 'Compared to the HC group, the 3 MCI groups (i.e., CVMCI, CKDMCI-3&4, and CKDMCI-H) showed a substantial decrease in the occipital alpha 2–3 power density.' (p. 5); '(2) the different calendar time, settings, and equipment used in the rsEEG recordings for the CDKMCI, CVMCI, and HC participants' (p. 8)
supporters.note: National archive, N = 85 (22 CKDMCI-3&4, 15 CKDMCI-H, 18 CVMCI, 30 HC); the record's 'sample size Not reported in source' is wrong. The reduction is in individually defined high alpha (alpha2 and alpha3), occipital in all three MCI groups (Bonferroni-corrected post hoc p < 0.001; Cohen's d for occipital alpha2 0.61, 1.04 and 1.37); alpha1 was not reduced versus controls except temporally in CKDMCI-3&4. CVMCI patients were recorded about one month after a stroke; the CKDMCI-3&4 data were reused from Lizio 2018; controls came from other centres, and the authors list different calendar time, settings and equipment across groups as a limitation, which confounds any patient-versus-control difference. Retrospective and cross-sectional.

supporters.quote: 'thus indicating a decrease of alpha coupling between these areas in the MCI group compared to their healthy counterpart.' (p. 7); exclusion criterion '(3) studies involving psychiatric and or neurologic diseases (e.g., Parkinson’s disease, vascular disease, Huntington’s disease, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, psychiatric illness, diabetes mellitus) were excluded' (p. 4)
supporters.note: Meta-analysis of 12 resting M/EEG connectivity studies in sensor space (327 HC, 379 MCI), mixing coherence, PLI, PLV and AEC. Small effects (d about -0.25): the temporo-parietal result is stable on leave-one-out (I2 = 1.11%), the fronto-parietal one is not. Parkinson's and vascular disease studies were excluded, so it gives no aetiology breadth, as the record already states; it sustains the alpha-band reduction in a second measurement family only. The record says the source is silent on non-alpha bands, but the Results report null pooled synchrony differences for theta (fronto-parietal p = 0.053), delta and beta. The abstract gives temporo-parietal d = -0.26 and fronto-parietal d = -0.25, whereas the Results give temporo-parietal d = -0.250 and fronto-parietal d = -0.260.

supporters.quote: Searched for a comparison with healthy controls: none. 'We enrolled 20 sporadic PD-MCI patients [...] and 10 MCI patients without Parkinsonism' (p. 2); 'The coherence values of whole-brain, FF, FT, FP, FPL, and FPR in PD-MCI were smaller than that in MCI without Parkinsonism.' (p. 2); 'MMSE scores showed a correlation with whole-brain coherence (r = 0.761).' (p. 3)
supporters.note: Nara pilot cohort with no healthy control group, so it cannot show reduced alpha in MCI relative to controls. It reports a within-PD-MCI correlation between alpha whole-brain coherence and MMSE, and lower coherence in PD-MCI than in non-parkinsonian MCI (band not stated in Table 1; several reported SDs exceed their means, e.g. whole-brain 0.377 +/- 0.490). The between-group result is an aetiology difference, not a shared signature. Cross-sectional, MCI defined by memory complaints with MMSE 24 to 30. Directionally consistent with alpha desynchronisation tracking severity, but it does not report the result the statement makes.

narrowed_wording: At group level, MCI shows reduced resting upper-alpha activity relative to controls in two measurement families: lower high-frequency alpha (alpha2 and alpha3) spectral power in two small EEG studies (P-450, P-398) and weaker alpha-band inter-regional synchrony in a meta-analysis of 12 M/EEG studies (P-453, d about -0.25). The two power studies saw the reduction in MCI of several aetiologies (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, chronic kidney disease, cerebrovascular), but that breadth rests on those two studies alone and is not itself a convergence; total alpha power was not reduced in P-450.
reasoning: Only P-398 supports the statement as the review states it. P-450 supports a narrower form (reduced high-alpha sub-band and alpha2/alpha1 ratio, total alpha unchanged). P-453 supports the alpha band in a second measurement family but by design gives no aetiology breadth. P-890 has no control group and reports no MCI-versus-control reduction; it should not count as a supporter, so the Table A1 count of 4 falls to 3 at most. The defining clause, 'cross-aetiology MCI signature', therefore rests on two small studies (N = 36 and N = 85, the second with patients and controls recorded on different equipment), below the three-study bar: if the review keeps that clause as the convergence, the verdict is fails. What three independent datasets do sustain is reduced upper-alpha activity in MCI versus controls, in spectral power and in inter-regional synchrony, which is the narrowed wording. Record details not borne out by the sources: P-398's sample size is reported (N = 85); both power studies report Bonferroni-adjusted p-values; P-453's Results do report the non-alpha bands (all null), which bears on the clause the record dropped as unsupported; and P-890 adds no MCI-versus-control evidence.
